absent: Full definitions of rcu_data, rcu_node, rcu_state, and nocb mask and mutex layout beyond referenced fields.
Main loops and wakeup protocols for grace, nocb group, nocb callback, core, and expedited worker threads.
Detailed semantics of QS reporting, urgency suppression, barrier entrainment, callback advancement, bypass flushing, and overload detection.
Hierarchy geometry derivation, fanout constants, boot parameter defaults, and per CPU initialization content.
Tick dependency mechanics, softirq versus kthread callback dispatch, and polled grace completion polling.
Power notifier registration, suspend ordering, and expedited control interactions.
Tracing, lockdep, stall detection, and torture or debug option behaviors.

findings.text: Externally visible CPU lifecycle helpers cover bringing a CPU online, reporting it starting, reporting it dead, migrating its callbacks, accounting it dead, tracing its dying transition, and taking it offline.

Early bringup plus scheduler transition plus lazy async hurry and relax plus expedited poll starter plus update oddness announcer are visible outside this unit for boot, power, and grace coordination.
Fanout force mask updates for online and offline episodes are protected by the leaf node lock with interrupt state saved and restored around the bit change.

Starting path acquires the global offline lock, then the global barrier lock, then the leaf node lock, releases the barrier lock before finishing expedited mask work, and uses interrupt save only on the forced QS report path.

Dead reporting holds the global offline lock together with the leaf node lock under interrupt disable, performs any pending QS report before clearing the initnext mask, then releases in reverse order.

Callback migration starts under the global barrier lock with interrupts off, then takes the destination nocb lock and destination node lock, drops the barrier lock early while keeping interrupts off, and follows separate release plus wake paths for offloaded versus regular destinations.
Nocb thread creation serializes group thread startup with the group mutex and serializes the failure deoffload path with the global nocb mutex, publishing both thread pointers with ordered writes.
Grace thread publication holds the root node lock with interrupts off while resetting activity timestamps and then publishing the thread pointer with release ordering before wakeup.
Polled expedited start conditions locking on whether initialization has run: it takes the node poll lock with interrupt save only after init, otherwise samples and queues without that lock.

Per CPU nocb startup stays idle until the scheduler is fully active and nocb setup is done, skips when a callback thread already exists, creates the group thread on demand with optional FIFO priority, then creates the CPU callback thread, wakes it when offloaded else parks it, optionally applies boost priority, publishes both pointers, and on creation failure deoffloads an offloaded CPU and clears its nocb mask under the global mutex.
One build variant of per CPU nocb startup intentionally provides no behavior and returns immediately.
Deferred QS initialization has two build variants: one arms a hard interrupt work item for deferred QS handling inside per CPU state, while the other leaves per CPU state unchanged.
Per node nocb initialization has two build variants: one prepares two grace wait queues for nocb operation, while the other performs no initialization.
Online handling adds the CPU bit to its leaf fanout force mask and, unless still in the inactive scheduler phase, clears the RCU tick dependency after stop machine work.

Starting handling runs once per online episode, records the CPU as started, joins normal and expedited initnext masks, increments total CPU count only for newly seen CPUs with release ordering, snapshots grace sequence and state, checks for offline induced wrap, and forces a QS report when the arriving CPU is still marked as blocking.

Dead handling requires interrupts off, drains deferred nocb wakeups and preempt deferred QS work, snapshots offline grace sequence and state, reports a QS before removing the CPU from initnext when it was blocking, then clears the started flag.

Migration leaves offloaded sources and empty callback lists untouched, otherwise entrains barrier state, advances source and destination segments to reuse recent grace periods, merges the source list into the current CPU list, disables the source list, validates overload and count consistency, wakes the destination appropriately, and wakes the grace thread when advancement made progress.

Dead accounting decrements the online CPU count under an exclusive writer expectation and clears the tick dependency, offline handling removes the CPU from the leaf force mask and sets the tick dependency for stop machine speed, and dying handling only emits a trace distinguishing whether the outgoing CPU was blocking a grace period.

Power handling hurries asynchronous work and expedites grace periods on hibernation or suspend prepare, relaxes both on post hibernation or post suspend, ignores other actions, and always reports successful notification handling.
Asynchronous hurry and relax adjust a global nesting counter upward and downward respectively, but only in builds with lazy callback support.

Grace thread bringup marks the scheduler fully active, creates the grace thread with optional FIFO priority, resets grace activity timestamps before publishing the thread pointer, wakes the thread, expects a single online CPU, then starts the local nocb thread plus node and core threads and the expedited worker.

Scheduler startup verifies single CPU and no context switches, exercises sync primitives, copies the global grace sequence into every node current and needed counters with interrupts off, then advances scheduler state out of early boot and retests primitives.

Single hierarchy setup validates level count, derives level bases and fanout spreads, initializes nodes leaves upward with per level lock classes, sequence values, empty masks, clamped CPU ranges, group identity and parent links with a null parent at the root, blocked lists, nocb state, expedited queues and locks and poll work, then binds each possible CPU to its leaf by range scan while linking barrier state and initializing per CPU data.

Thread priority setup enforces a higher minimum when boost and torture support interact, otherwise enforces boost minimum and clamps the value into the zero to ninety nine range, logging whenever the input is altered.

Top level initialization runs early tests, announces the build, sanitizes priority, builds geometry and the node hierarchy, optionally dumps the layout, optionally enables softirq handling, registers power handling, prepares and starts and onlines the boot CPU while still single CPU, allocates grace and sync workqueues, derives the overload threshold from the high mark when unspecified, kick starts early polled grace periods, retests primitives, and initializes generic task callback lists.

Polled expedited start samples the current expedited state, and when that state has not yet completed it stores the requested sequence in the local node and queues that node poll work on the grace workqueue, returning the sampled cookie in all cases.

Boot announcement selects a preemptible versus non preemptible message and then reports non default fanout and leaf tuning, CPU restriction, boost settings, callback limits and watermarks, scan and enlistment delays, kick behavior, debug slowdowns, patience clamping into a bounded millisecond interval converted to jiffies, softirq versus thread dispatch, extended QS debugging, and update level expedited and stall settings.
Expedited work carrier combines an unsigned sequence cookie with an embedded kernel thread work item for deferred execution.

Observed node state spans a main lock plus a force scan lock, grace sequence plus needed plus completed QS tracking, normal and expedited masks with init variants, CPU range bounds, grouping number plus mask plus parent link plus level, a blocked task list, nocb grace queues, four expedited wait queues with associated locks and poll request state and poll work, and a thread mutex.

Observed per CPU state spans the owning leaf node pointer, group mask, segmented callback list, started and beenonline flags, nocb group and callback thread pointers with associated mutexes and masks, deferred QS work, online and offline grace snapshots, QS pending flags, overload state, and barrier linkage.
Kernel thread execution uses five ordered conditions from stopped through running, waiting, off CPU, and yielding, with the maximum value equal to the yielding value.

A CPU episode moves from prepare to a once only starting join, to online force mask membership, then through offline removal with tick dependency set, dead QS handling and callback migration, and dead accounting, with beenonline published by release store followed by a barrier before read side use.
Boot control moves from inactive where scheduler work is skipped, to init after node sequences are fixed, to fully active where grace and nocb thread creation is allowed.

Nocb thread disposition ensures the group thread before the CPU callback thread, wakes the callback thread when its CPU is offloaded and parks it otherwise, and returns to non offloaded membership on creation failure.

Boot enters through top level init on a single CPU, grace thread creation as a pre SMP initcall, and scheduler startup transition, while runtime enters through CPU hotplug hooks, the power notifier, and polled expedited start which tolerates pre init callers.

Thread allocation failures emit a once only warning noting that out of memory becomes expected behavior, and the nocb error path additionally warns when a post boot CPU still queues callbacks while holding the global nocb mutex to avoid imbalance from reclaim.

Unexpected mask membership warns: an arriving CPU still marked blocking forces a late QS report, a departing CPU with pending expedited QS warns, and migration warns on an online source, on bypass flush failure, on empty versus count inconsistency, and on callbacks left behind after source disable.

Bringup validates assumptions by warning on more than one online CPU, on missing grace or sync workqueues, on unexpected context switches during scheduler startup, and by aborting when the computed level count falls outside the supported range.
Thread state encodings are small integers with stopped at zero, running at one, waiting at two, off CPU at three, yielding at four, and maximum also at four.
